Claim: Low-resource ASR is multidimensional and cannot be reduced to labeled hours.
VerificationBasis: Core 60 verified-primary and verified-secondary benchmark corpus and evaluation anchors
CounterEvidenceOrLimits: The exact dimensions differ by language domain and deployment target
AllowedWording: Low-resource ASR should be defined as a multidimensional reliability condition
OverclaimRisk: Low if tied to matrices and RQ1

Claim: Foundation speech models improve the starting point of low-resource ASR but shift the bottleneck toward adaptation data quality and evaluation rather than eliminating the bottleneck.
VerificationBasis: Core 60 foundation model anchors with adaptation and evaluation matrices
CounterEvidenceOrLimits: Some models are not pure ASR and some sources are emerging or translation-centric
AllowedWording: Foundation models reshape the low-resource bottleneck rather than remove it
OverclaimRisk: Medium if phrased as universal performance guarantee

Claim: Data-centric strategies remain necessary in the foundation-model era because corpus quality filtering normalization metadata and validation shape downstream model behavior.
VerificationBasis: Core corpus and data-pipeline evidence plus data-centric matrix
CounterEvidenceOrLimits: Data strategies vary by domain and benchmark and should not be presented as universal recipes
AllowedWording: Data quality and documentation remain central even with strong pretrained models
OverclaimRisk: Low if linked to dataset quality and validation

Claim: Adaptation effectiveness is conditional: the best strategy depends on target-language data domain mismatch language relatedness compute budget and risk of forgetting.
VerificationBasis: Core method anchors plus ASR-specific Interspeech adaptation evidence
CounterEvidenceOrLimits: PEFT evidence is uneven and some anchors are NLP method papers
AllowedWording: No adaptation method should be recommended without specifying conditions
OverclaimRisk: Medium if method anchors are treated as direct ASR proof

Claim: Pseudo-labeling and KD can expand supervision but their reliability depends on teacher quality uncertainty confidence filtering teacher agreement and language or domain mismatch.
VerificationBasis: Core self-training pseudo-labeling and KD entries plus Block E matrix
CounterEvidenceOrLimits: Teacher disagreement and calibration are not always reported consistently
AllowedWording: Pseudo-labels should be treated as noisy supervision requiring validation
OverclaimRisk: Medium if pseudo-labels are framed as equivalent to human labels

Claim: Evaluation based only on pooled WER/CER is insufficient for low-resource ASR because it can hide dialect domain orthographic demographic and hallucination-related failure modes.
VerificationBasis: Verified benchmark fairness robustness and hallucination-risk evidence
CounterEvidenceOrLimits: Hallucination and LLM-assisted evidence is partly secondary or watchlist and should be bounded
AllowedWording: Report pooled scores alongside language dialect domain and normalization details
OverclaimRisk: Medium if WER/CER are dismissed rather than contextualized

Claim: Multimodal AVSR SpeechLM and LLM-assisted ASR are promising future directions but they introduce new evaluation risks such as hallucination over-correction contextual bias modality mismatch and compute opacity.
VerificationBasis: Core multimodal and hallucination evidence plus watchlist restricted to emerging directions
CounterEvidenceOrLimits: Several LLM and contextual benchmark sources are arXiv watchlist only
AllowedWording: These methods are promising but should be presented as future-facing and evaluation-sensitive
OverclaimRisk: High if watchlist papers are used as settled evidence

Claim: The field needs a reproducible future agenda built around transparent datasets dialect-aware benchmarks compute-efficient adaptation constrained LLM correction/rescoring multimodal robustness and community-aware resource development.
VerificationBasis: Core evidence plus documentation candidate file for future agenda support
CounterEvidenceOrLimits: Documentation-support sources are methodological rather than ASR evidence
AllowedWording: Future work should connect each recommendation to a demonstrated gap
OverclaimRisk: Medium if agenda becomes speculative or Pashto-centered
